topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Hallmarks and Progression
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by presenting the learning outcomes, the multistep colorectal tumor progression model, and the conceptual framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth Signal Autonomy and Evasion of Inhibitory Signals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades like Wnt, RTKs, and TGF-beta drive independent proliferation and overcome inhibitory signals.

topics.label: Differentiation Block in Hematological and Epithelial Cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how impaired terminal differentiation prevents cells from exiting the cell cycle, using examples from leukemias and colonic crypts.

topics.label: Resistance to Apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through mutations in p53 and the dysregulation of mitochondrial apoptotic proteins like Bax and BCL2.

topics.label: Replicative Immortality and Senescence Bypass
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cells normally enter senescence in response to telomere erosion and stress, and how cancer cells bypass this limit through telomerase activation to achieve immortalization.

topics.label: Deregulation of Cellular Metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the emergence of complex cancer hallmarks and detail how tumors rewire cellular metabolism via aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite accumulation.

topics.label: Induction of Tumor Angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the requirement, timing, and molecular balancing act governing new blood vessel formation to supply oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Detection of Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the biological stages, detection strategies, and clonal genetics underlying the dissemination and colonization of cancer cells at distant sites.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides closing framing by summarizing the collective nature of cancer hallmarks, discussing recent literature, and opening the floor to questions.
